title: Plurimath conformance case group, for a call other than default-options render
description: One file of conformance cases recording a call the gem answered with something OTHER than a plain parse-then-render: a render method invoked with a non-default option, a configuration, or an argument beyond the input itself. `cases/1` and `cases/2` can only ever record `Formula#to_<target>` with no arguments — there is no field either schema offers for `formatter:`, `intent:`, `split_on_linebreak:`, `display_style:`, or `evaluate(bindings)`. This is a SEPARATE payload kind from `cases/*`, the same way `rejections/1` sits beside them rather than folding into them (see that schema's description): its cases carry an extra `call` field naming what was invoked and with what, and its `schema` value names a KIND rather than an input format, exactly as `rejections/1` and `provenance/2` do, because `call.method` — not the input's own notation — is what varies within one payload. `call.method` is deliberately a narrow enum today (`number_formatter` only, TODO.plan/feature-roadmap.md's B1 slice): the other five call kinds the roadmap names (`intent`, `split_on_linebreak`, `display_style`, `to_display`, `evaluate`) are each a later schema version's addition, not a guess made now about a shape none of them has been measured against yet.

schema.description: A kind, like `provenance` and `rejections`, not an input format: the format is carried per payload in `input_format`, and per case in each case's own `input_format`.

group.description: Feature group; matches the file name without its extension. A schema cannot see the file name, so scripts/validate.rb enforces the match.

input_format.description: Agrees with every case's `input_format`; scripts/validate.rb reconciles the two.

targets.description: Output formats every case in this group carries an outcome for, under the same call. Still one list for the whole group, and still exhaustive per case, exactly as in `cases/2`.

class_name.description: A Plurimath model class, with the `Plurimath::` prefix stripped.

error_category.description: What rendering this target did, at the coarseness the gem's public boundary exposes. Identical in meaning to `cases/2`'s definition of the same name: `parse_error` is the only value a render failure can carry, because `Math::Formula#to_*` funnels every render-time failure through `wrap_render_error`. A call whose own arguments are rejected before rendering is attempted (an unsupported `formatter:`/`locale:` value, say) is a different failure this schema version does not yet record; every case here is one where the call itself was accepted.

call.description: What was invoked, beyond a plain parse-then-render. `method` names the KIND of call, not a Ruby method name by itself — `number_formatter` covers every `to_<target>(formatter: ...)` invocation across every target in `targets`, because the same formatter is applied uniformly to each. `args` is deliberately free-form (like a node's own `options`/`attributes` fields already are): typing every call kind's argument shape into this schema would fix a shape not yet settled for kinds this version does not cover, and even for `number_formatter` the argument names are the gem's own keyword names, not independently invented ones, so a reader maps them straight onto its own constructor.

outcome.description: What one target did with this case, under `call`: exactly one of a rendering or a refusal. Structurally identical to `cases/2`'s `outcome` — see that schema's description for why `oneOf` and the nested `type: object` are both load-bearing here.

output.description: Exactly the bytes the gem produced for this target, under `call`. Compared byte for byte.

id.description: Stable identifier, unique within the group; scripts/validate.rb enforces the uniqueness, which one schema item cannot see of its siblings.

input_format.description: Equals the group's `input_format`; scripts/validate.rb enforces the agreement.

preprocessed.description: The input after the format's preprocessing pass, which may shift offsets.

expected.description: Outcome per target format, under `call`. The keys are exactly the group's `targets`, exactly as in `cases/2`; scripts/validate.rb checks the correspondence.

parse_tree.description: The parser's tree, serialized as plain data. Numbers and booleans are excluded deliberately: no parse tree has ever produced one, so a new scalar kind should be a validation failure rather than a silent shape change.

node.description: A Plurimath::Math::Core node: its class, and its instance variables serialized by name.

object_field_value.description: An object-valued field is either a nested node or a plain map such as `options` or `attributes`. A `class` key means it claims to be a node, so it must be a well-formed one.
